title: The Cardiac Cycle
subject: Physiology
description: Example: the cardiac cycle, heart sounds, and the ECG.

cards.cloze: The cardiac cycle lasts about {{0.8 seconds}} at a heart rate of {{75 beats}} per minute. {{Systole}} occupies about {{0.3 seconds}}, while {{diastole}} occupies about {{0.5 seconds}}.
The normal cardiac impulse originates in the {{sinoatrial (SA) node}}, located in the wall of the {{right atrium}}.
The impulse is delayed at the {{atrioventricular (AV) node}} by about {{0.1 seconds}}, allowing the {{atria}} to empty blood into the ventricles before ventricular contraction begins.
During the period of {{isovolumetric contraction}}, {{all four valves}} are closed and ventricular pressure rises without any change in {{volume}}.

The {{end-diastolic volume}} is normally about {{120 mL}}, and the {{end-systolic volume}} is about {{50 mL}}. The {{stroke volume}}, which is the difference between them, is therefore about {{70 mL}}.
The first heart sound is caused by closure of the {{atrioventricular valves}}, and the second heart sound is caused by closure of the {{semilunar valves}}.
{{Cardiac output}} equals {{stroke volume}} multiplied by {{heart rate}}, and in a resting adult it is about {{5 L/min}}.
The {{P wave}} represents {{atrial depolarization}}, the {{QRS complex}} represents {{ventricular depolarization}}, and the {{T wave}} represents {{ventricular repolarization}}.
